learning.title: A migration that needs a drain takes bakery_app offline: stop every app service, and recover a timed-out pre-deploy by redeploying the api
learning.trigger: deploy-qa prints "QA migration needs a drain" or the api pre-deploy fails APPLICATION_DATABASE_DRAIN_REQUIRED; or the api pre-deploy was killed at its time limit; or new bakery_app connections fail while the old api still serves; or a deploy job reports TIMEOUT or ROLLOUT TIMEOUT.
learning.mistake: Stopped only the dispatcher before a drain migration; ran GRANT CONNECT by hand to repair a revoked role; or redeployed immediately after a TIMEOUT without checking whether Railway was still progressing.
learning.rule: Some migrations need bakery_app offline (withApplicationDatabaseDrain, row in bakery.application_migration_drain). The pre-deploy step records the current grants, revokes CONNECT on the database from public and bakery_app, counts bakery_app sessions and fails APPLICATION_DATABASE_DRAIN_REQUIRED if any remain; its finally block restores the recorded grants. The old api keeps serving, which is safe. The pre-deploy runs while the old api and the dispatcher both hold bakery_app sessions, so stopping only the dispatcher is not enough. Procedure (planned QA downtime): (1) railway down -s dispatcher --yes, then railway down -s api --yes. (2) Confirm zero sessions: railway ssh -s Postgres -- psql -U postgres -tAc "select count(*) from pg_stat_activity where usename='bakery_app'" prints 0. (3) railway redeploy -s api --yes; the pre-deploy drains, migrates and restores CONNECT; wait for SUCCESS. (4) railway redeploy -s dispatcher --yes; wait for SUCCESS. Stop a worker first if it holds runs.

Pre-deploy has a 900 s limit and the container is killed at it, so finally never runs. A kill in the middle of a drain leaves CONNECT revoked from bakery_app while the old api still serves, and its new connections fail. Detect it after a failed or timed-out api deploy: railway ssh -s Postgres -- psql -U postgres -tAc "select has_database_privilege('bakery_app','bakery','CONNECT')" prints f when revoked. Recover with railway redeploy -s api --yes: the next pre-deploy restores the recorded grants. Never GRANT by hand while a bakery.application_migration_drain row exists; the bootstrap also refuses to re-grant CONNECT while that row is there.

Read deploy timeouts by their wording. "TIMEOUT after 35 min without progress" means one deployment sat on a single status for 35 minutes: look at it in the Railway dashboard before redeploying, because a merely slow deployment changes status and does not trip this bound. "ROLLOUT TIMEOUT after 120 min" means the whole rollout, not one service, ran out of budget: look for a build-queue backlog across the project rather than one wedged service. An older total-duration bound once reported a service TIMEOUT while Railway went on to promote that deployment, leaving QA on the previous SHA until the next merge; see railway-deploy-without-github-app.

verification.command: railway ssh -s Postgres -- psql -U postgres -tAc "select count(*) from pg_stat_activity where usename='bakery_app'"
verification.requirement: Record 0 sessions before the api redeploy, t for CONNECT after it, the api and dispatcher deployments at SUCCESS, and /health/ready reporting the expected version.

learning.boundary: A drain is planned downtime, never part of a rolling release. Railway ssh needs a registered key and the other flags in railway-ssh-key-and-pid1-env. The skill-object-storage switch tool reuses the same drain row and advisory lock and refuses to proceed while any bakery_app connection remains.
